title: contrib: hook improvements
description:
## Summary

Format clang in place instead of just alerting + reject assisted-by in commit messages akin to signoffs.

## Purpose

The formatting check adds unnecessary friction where a developer needs to manually run the formatter after the alert rather than having the hook alert + just format in place. 

The assisted-by in commit messages line is easy to miss in reviews and has already slipped in a few times. We should apply the standard consistently here.

## Checklist

Please read https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/NetworkManager/NetworkManager/-/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md before opening the merge request. In particular, check that:

- [x] The subject for all commits is concise, explanatory, and includes a prefix indicating the area of code changed (e.g., "nmcli: ", "core: ")
- [x] The message for all commits explains the reason for the change
- [x] The source is properly formatted
- [x] Any relevant documentation is up to date
- [x] You have added unit tests if applicable
- [x] The NEWS file is updated when the change deserves to be mentioned, for example for new features, behavior changes, API deprecations, etc.
author: josie
diff:
--- contrib/scripts/check-commit-message.sh
+++ contrib/scripts/check-commit-message.sh
@@ -23,19 +23,31 @@ usage() {
     printf 'Check commit messages against the rules from CONTRIBUTING.md.\n'
 }
 
-check_message() {
+check_trailer() {
     local source="$1"
     local message="$2"
+    local trailer="$3"
+    local reason="$4"
     local hit
 
-    hit="$(printf '%s\n' "$message" | grep -i '^Signed-off-by:')" || return 0
+    hit="$(printf '%s\n' "$message" | grep -i "^$trailer:")" || return 0
 
-    printf '%s: do not use "Signed-off-by:" lines, they have no meaning for NetworkManager (see CONTRIBUTING.md)\n' "$source" >&2
+    printf '%s: do not use "%s:" lines, %s (see CONTRIBUTING.md)\n' "$source" "$trailer" "$reason" >&2
     sed 's/^/> /' <<<"$hit" >&2
     printf '\n' >&2
     return 1
 }
 
+check_message() {
+    local ret=0
+
+    check_trailer "$1" "$2" "Signed-off-by" \
+        "they have no meaning for NetworkManager" || ret=1
+    check_trailer "$1" "$2" "Assisted-by" \
+        "NetworkManager does not record tool assistance in commit messages" || ret=1
+    return "$ret"
+}
+
 get_ci_base() {
     local base
 
--- .pre-commit-config.yaml
+++ .pre-commit-config.yaml
@@ -10,7 +10,7 @@ repos:
     hooks:
       - id: nm-clang-format
         name: clang-format (CI version, container)
-        entry: ./contrib/scripts/nm-code-format-container.sh -n
+        entry: ./contrib/scripts/nm-code-format-container.sh -i

title: kitemviews: Leave the selection alone when the middle button is pressed
description:
Holding the middle button down and dragging drew a rubber band and selected
whatever it covered, and a middle press on its own cleared the selection. The
middle button opens an item in a new tab, so it has nothing to say about what
is selected.

onPress answers for the left, right, back and forward buttons and fell through
for the middle one. Its caller reads that as nobody having claimed the press
and starts a rubber band, which is where the selection box came from. Answer
for the middle button too, next to the back and forward buttons that are
turned down for the same reason.

Opening in a new tab is untouched. That happens on release, from the item the
release position points at.

title: Docs: Explain artifact object storage size reconciliation
description:
## What does this MR do?

Adds a troubleshooting section, "Object storage usage does not match reported artifact size", to `doc/administration/cicd/job_artifacts_troubleshooting.md`.

The section documents:

- That the artifact size GitLab reports (projects API with `statistics=true`, GraphQL `buildArtifactsSize`) is calculated from database records, not bucket contents.
- The known causes of a bucket being larger than the reported total:
  - The GitLab 16.1/16.2 expired-artifact deletion bug (existing section on this page).
  - Orphaned objects from project deletion in GitLab 19.2 and earlier (https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/issues/604201, fixed in 19.3 for new deletions only).
  - Asynchronous deletion queueing.
  - Non-current object versions retained by bucket versioning.
- The limitation that the `gitlab:cleanup:list/delete_orphan_job_artifact_final_objects` Rake tasks scan only `@final` paths, and that no supported tooling exists for legacy date-based paths (contact Support).

## References

Motivated by two support escalations where customers could not reconcile hundreds of TB of divergence between bucket usage and GitLab-reported artifact size:

- https://gitlab.com/gitlab-com/request-for-help/-/work_items/5282 (internal, GitLab Dedicated, 1.22 PB bucket vs ~487 TB reported)
- https://gitlab.com/gitlab-com/request-for-help/-/work_items/5220 (internal, Self-Managed 18.11, 223 TB bucket vs ~32 TB reported)

Note for reviewers: the statement that https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/issues/604201 is fixed in 19.3 is sourced from the support investigation in the second escalation. Please verify the fix version before merge.

## Author's checklist

- [x] Follow the [Documentation Guidelines](https://docs.gitlab.com/development/documentation/) and [Style Guide](https://docs.gitlab.com/development/documentation/styleguide/).
- [ ] Technical writer review
author: gyoachum
diff:
--- doc/administration/cicd/job_artifacts_troubleshooting.md
+++ doc/administration/cicd/job_artifacts_troubleshooting.md
@@ -293,6 +293,38 @@ The following applies to all types of GitLab deployment:
     35/13/35135aaa6cc23891b40cb3f378c53a17a1127210ce60e125ccf03efcfdaec458/@final/1a/1a/5abfa4ec66f1cc3b681a4d430b8b04596cbd636f13cdff44277211778f26,201,1711616743796587
     ```
 
+### Object storage usage does not match reported artifact size
+
+The job artifact size that GitLab reports is calculated from database records,
+not from the contents of your object storage bucket. To retrieve the reported
+size, use the [projects API](../../api/projects.md) with `statistics=true`, or
+the `buildArtifactsSize` field in the GraphQL project statistics.
+
+Your artifacts bucket can use more storage than the reported total.
+Possible causes:
+
+- Orphaned objects from expired artifacts that were not deleted in GitLab 16.1 and 16.2.
+  For more information, see
+  [`@final` artifacts not deleted from object store](#final-artifacts-not-deleted-from-object-store).
+- Orphaned objects from deleted projects. In GitLab 19.2 and earlier, deleting a
+  project could remove job artifact records from the database without deleting the
+  corresponding objects from object storage. For more information, see
+  [issue 604201](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/issues/604201).
+  GitLab 19.3 and later prevents new orphaned objects, but does not remove
+  orphaned objects that already exist.
+- Objects queued for deletion. Deleted artifact records are queued and their
+  objects removed asynchronously, so recently deleted artifacts might still be
+  in the bucket.
+- Non-current object versions. If bucket versioning is enabled, deleted objects
+  can be retained as non-current versions until a lifecycle policy removes them.
+
+To identify and remove orphaned objects, use the
+[orphaned job artifact Rake tasks](#list-orphaned-job-artifacts). These Rake
+tasks scan only objects stored under `@final` paths. Artifacts stored under
+legacy date-based paths are not scanned, and no supported tooling exists to
+identify orphaned objects under those paths. If a large discrepancy remains
+after you run the Rake tasks, contact GitLab Support.
+
 ### List projects and builds with artifacts with a specific expiration (or no expiration)

title: window: Recalculate sticky state after monitor layout changes
description:
## What does this MR do?

Fixes a residual issue after !5228 (merged) where secondary-monitor windows remain "bound to a workspace" after a multi→single→multi RDP reconnect sequence, even with `workspaces-only-on-primary` enabled.

With `workspaces-only-on-primary` enabled, windows on non-primary monitors should be sticky (`on_all_workspaces = TRUE`), i.e. visible on all workspaces. After the reconnect sequence, these windows incorrectly retain `on_all_workspaces = FALSE` and disappear when switching workspaces.

## Root cause

The sticky state of a window is a derived value. It is computed by `should_be_on_all_workspaces()`, which with `workspaces-only-on-primary` enabled ends up reading the primary state of the logical monitor the window is currently on:

```c
if (meta_prefs_get_workspaces_only_on_primary () &&
    !window->unmanaging &&
    window->monitor &&
    !meta_window_is_on_primary_monitor (window)) /* window->monitor->is_primary */
  return TRUE;
```

`meta_window_on_all_workspaces_changed()` therefore has to be called whenever any of these inputs change, otherwise `window->on_all_workspaces` keeps its stale value. In the monitor-change path the only call site is `meta_window_update_monitor()`, and it is guarded by a _pointer_ comparison:

```c
g_set_object (&old, window->monitor);
META_WINDOW_GET_CLASS (window)->update_main_monitor (window, flags);
if (old != window->monitor)
  {
    meta_window_on_all_workspaces_changed (window);
    ...
  }
```

So the sticky state is re-derived only when `window->monitor` changes identity, not when the `is_primary` state of that monitor changes.

That is exactly what happens on a monitor layout change: `MetaLogicalMonitor` objects are reused rather than recreated. `meta_monitor_manager_update_logical_monitors()` calls `meta_logical_monitor_update()`, which matches on number, rect, transform, scale and monitor specs - but not on `is_primary` - and never writes `is_primary` itself. The primary flag is assigned afterwar
author: YingjieLiu
diff:
--- src/core/window.c
+++ src/core/window.c
@@ -4257,6 +4257,16 @@ out:
   g_assert (!window->monitor ||
             g_list_find (meta_monitor_manager_get_logical_monitors (monitor_manager),
                          window->monitor));
+
+  /* Logical monitor objects are reused across configuration changes, so
+   * window->monitor may still point at the same object even though its
+   * "is primary" state changed. With workspaces-only-on-primary the sticky
+   * state derives from that state, and it is otherwise only re-derived when
+   * window->monitor changes identity, so re-evaluate it unconditionally
+   * here, once the new configuration is fully in place. This is a no-op if
+   * the derived state didn't actually change.
+   */
+  meta_window_on_all_workspaces_changed (window);
 }
 
 void

title: js: Add incremental JavaScript type checking
description:
This merge request adds an incremental typechecking setup for GNOME Shell's JavaScript code and generated type definitions for GObject Introspection libraries.

It does not convert any JavaScript code to TypeScript. TypeScript is used only as a static checker for existing JavaScript through JSDoc and per-file `// @ts-check` directives.

JavaScript files that are not annotated with `// @ts-check` continue to be treated as unchecked JavaScript just as before.

## Incremental JavaScript typechecking

The new `js/tsconfig.json` configuration:

- Allows JavaScript input without emitting compiled files.
- Keeps project-wide JavaScript checking disabled, making it opt-in rather than forcing type checking on every file.
- Enables `noImplicitAny` for files that explicitly opt in.
- Disables default Node.js types
- Targets the JavaScript features used by GNOME Shell.

The primary motivating consumer is `js/ui/keyboard.js` in [GNOME Shell !4350](https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/gnome-shell/-/merge_requests/4350). That merge request uses `// @ts-check`, JSDoc, generated GIR definitions, and companion declarations to check the complete keyboard module with `noImplicitAny` enabled. This provides a practical example of incrementally checking a large existing GJS module without converting it to TypeScript.

This merge request provides the shared declarations required by that work:

- `js/misc/signals.d.ts` describes the public `EventEmitter` API used throughout `keyboard.js`, including signal connection, disconnection, and emission.
- `js/types/gjs-extensions.d.ts` describes APIs added dynamically by the GJS runtime or `js/ui/environment.js`. These include the legacy `imports.signals` global, tracked GObject signal helpers, Clutter actor iteration and easing helpers, GLib one-shot source helpers, and `Math.clamp()`.
- `js/types/gnome-shell-globals.d.ts` describes GNOME Shell's `global` object, translation functions, and logging functions.

title: xx-hotkey-v1: global hotkey protocol
description:
#### Requirements for merging

- [ ] Review
- [x] Implementations

This protocol lets a client choose and freely reconfigure its own global hotkeys: it requests a specific key combination and the compositor accepts it or denies it with a reason. The compositor stays the arbiter (it can deny, revoke at any time, apply any policy it wants), but within that the application manages its own bindings at runtime, with no out-of-band user configuration and no persisted compositor state.

This is the wayland equivalent of RegisterHotKey (Windows), RegisterEventHotKey (macOS) and XGrabKey (X11). Applications that depend on global hotkeys (launchers, push-to-talk, media controls, streaming software) currently either can't offer the feature on wayland or resort to workarounds.

## Why a wayland protocol rather than the portal?

* The trigger keysym is defined in the same numbering as the keymap delivered over wl_keyboard on that seat, with a specified layout-group matching rule. The portal's trigger strings have no keymap to resolve against, and the portal can't even return a stable parsable representation of the current binding.
* The compositor consumes the triggering key press, so the client has no input serial of its own. The pressed event carries one for xdg_activation_token_v1.set_serial, so raising a surface from a hotkey works through the normal activation path.
* No dependency on a running portal and D-Bus session, which users of many standalone compositors don't have.

## Relation to existing approaches

The action-registration model (GlobalShortcuts portal, hyprland-global-shortcuts-v1, the action-binder RFC !216) makes the user pick the trigger out-of-band. For cross-platform apps with in-app shortcut settings this inverts the UX of every other platform: the app can only suggest a trigger with no feedback on what got bound, can't rebind from its own UI, and depends on a compositor settings UI many compositors don't have.

Here, every request gets an explicit answer:

title: alsa-pcm: recover from stale driver state after S3 resume
description:
Some HDMI/HDA drivers (e.g. the Innosilicon "FantasyCard" GPU audio
device) return success from snd_pcm_start()/snd_pcm_resume() without
actually transitioning the PCM to RUNNING after system suspend. The
hw position stays stale, so snd_pcm_delay() keeps reporting a
persistently inflated delay that never exceeds max_resync. The
driver-node DLL then integrates this one-sided error and lowers the
resample ratio until it locks around 0.78, producing audible
crackling/buzzing that only stops when the stream ends.

Fix this on the driver (non-follower) path:

* do_prepare(): fully reset the rate adaptation state
  (next_time, base_time, err_avg, err_var, resync counters) and
  check the return value of spa_alsa_silence().
* do_start(): after a successful snd_pcm_start(), verify
  snd_pcm_avail(); if it fails (e.g. -EPIPE) the PCM did not
  actually run, so report the error and fall back to a full
  drop+prepare+start instead of feeding stale data to the graph.
* alsa_recover(): after snd_pcm_resume() succeeds, validate
  avail/delay against target before accepting it; a stale hw
  position leaving delay far above target is rejected and a full
  recovery is performed. Propagate do_start() errors.
* update_time(): on driver nodes, detect a sustained error whose
  magnitude stays below max_resync (which would otherwise never
  trigger the existing resync) and force a full resync.
* alsa_write_sync()/alsa_read_sync(): add the missing driver-node
  resync handling: force the buffer level back to target
  (snd_pcm_rewind/forward or silence) so err becomes 0, and do a
  full drop+prepare+start when the sustained-error detection fired.
* alsa_write_frames(): check the do_start() return value instead of
  ignoring it.

Tested on an Innosilicon Fantasy II-M (HDMI) machine with a 300s
test tone: 37 consecutive S3 suspend/resume cycles all recovered to
rate ~1.0 within a few seconds (previously the rate dived to 0.78
and produced persistent noise until playback was restarted).

title: Qt: split stashed preferences treatment in two steps
description:
When applying new preferences, the call to the function
prefs_modules_for_all_modules(module_prefs_unstash, (void *)&redissect_flags)
does two things at the same time:
- apply the new value for each stashed preference
- get the redissect_flags bitmap for later treatment
When the PREF_EFFECT_DISSECTION flag is set, we want to freeze the
packet list before performing the redissection. This can lead to an
unexpected state where a given dissector has the preference new value
applied but the redissection has not been performed yet. If this
preference has an associated memory allocation for example, it can lead
to a null pointer dereference.
To avoid this, iterate two times on the stashed preferences: first to
get the redissect_flags bitmap, then freeze the packet list if required,
and finally apply the stashed values.

Fixes #21380

(cherry picked from commit c17e8ddddfcdf09a6cfd4818d9595c12532f7d06)

	epan/prefs-int.h
	epan/prefs.c
	ui/qt/preferences_dialog.cpp

title: Add 8-up print layout
description:
## Summary

Add 8-up support to the Unix print dialog and print-to-file backend.

- Offer 8 pages per sheet for the file backend.
- Offer it for CUPS destinations only when `number-up-supported` contains 8.
- Render 8-up as a rotated 4 by 2 layout, matching the preview.

The CUPS choice is capability-gated because existing CUPS versions and IPP
destinations do not necessarily support 8. Companion server-side support is
being proposed in [OpenPrinting/cups#1672](https://github.com/OpenPrinting/cups/pull/1672).

The corresponding GTK 3 change is !10259; the two changes are independent.

## Testing

- `git diff --check`
- Built all changed printing implementation objects with Ninja, including the
  CUPS and file backends.
- Verified `ippContainsInteger()` with discrete values without and with 8, a
  list containing additional values, a range containing 8, and a missing
  attribute.
- Manually ran the print-to-file path with 8 selected. The resulting PDF had
  exactly one A4 sheet, and visual inspection confirmed pages 1 through 8 in
  the rotated 4 by 2 layout.

The CUPS runtime path was not exercised against a live CUPS or IPP destination
advertising 8-up support.

This merge request was developed with assistance from an LLM. I reviewed the
implementation and performed the checks listed above.

title: Draft: Allow security bot to access components from internal projects
description:
## What does this MR do and why?

Fixes https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/issues/603881

When a pipeline execution policy includes a CI/CD component hosted in an internal project, the security policy bot is denied access because the component resolution path does not consult the bot-access setting (`allows_pipeline_execution_policy_ci_config_access?`).

### Changes

1. **Component access check** (`ee/app/services/ee/ci/components/fetch_service.rb`): Add EE override for `FetchService` that checks the bot-access setting before denying access. This mirrors the existing EE override in `File::Project` for direct includes.

2. **Target project accessor** (`ee/lib/gitlab/ci/pipeline/pipeline_execution_policies/pipeline_context.rb`): Add public `target_project` method to expose the original pipeline target project. This is necessary because during nested includes (e.g., policy → policy-ci.yml → component), `requesting_project` changes to reflect the current include source, but `allows_pipeline_execution_policy_ci_config_access?` needs the original target project where the pipeline is running and where security policies are active.

## How to set up and validate locally

### Prerequisites

1. **Create an internal project to host the CI/CD component** (e.g., `my-group/component-project`)
   - Set visibility to **Internal**
   - Create a component file at `templates/my-component.yml`:
     ```yaml
     spec:
       inputs:
         stage:
           default: test
     ---
     component-job:
       stage: $[[ inputs.stage ]]
       script:
         - echo "Running component job"
     ```
   - Create a tag (e.g., `1.0.0`) for the component version

2. **Create a security policy project** (e.g., `my-group/security-policies`)
   - Create a pipeline execution policy that references your component:
     ```yaml
     # .gitlab/security-policies/policy.yml
     pipeline_execution_policy:
       - name: "Component Policy"
         enabled: true
         pipeline_config_strategy:

title: wrong editor answers when both are open
description:
### Context

This patch is part of a series that came out of building **KICAD_MCP**, an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server that lets
LLM agents drive a live KiCad session through KiCad's official IPC API — the
protobuf-over-socket interface that also backs `kicad-python`/`kipy`. The
agent does what a plugin would do, only continuously and headlessly: place
symbols and footprints, wire up hierarchical sheets, run ERC, update the PCB
from the schematic — all as `CreateItems` / `GetItems` / `UpdateItems` /
`SaveDocument` / … protobuf requests.

Driving the API at that intensity exercises paths no interactive session
hits: documents that are open but not displayed, sheets other than the active
one, both editors open against the same project, round-trips through the
clipboard S-expression format, and error paths that must come back as
protobuf statuses rather than dialogs (an IPC client cannot click "OK", so
any modal dialog reached from a handler hangs the client). A typical session
that surfaced several of the bugs in this series at once:

> create a sub-sheet → place a resistor on it while the root sheet is
> displayed → save all → run ERC from `kicad-cli` — each step crossed a
> different bug fixed below.

The branches are cut against `master` and are independent of each other
unless the section says otherwise.

### Authorship

The code was co-authored and reviewed with LLM assistance (**Claude-Fable-5** and **GLM**-5.1), under human direction, code-revision, and validated by
a human against a live KiCad build. Every branch compiles clean (Release,
`-DKICAD_BUILD_QA_TESTS=ON`) and went through two adversarial review rounds
before submission.

---

**Function:** `validateDocumentInternal` in `API_HANDLER_SCH` /
`API_HANDLER_PCB` / `API_HANDLER_FOOTPRINT`, and the
`API_HANDLER_EDITOR::validateDocument` wrapper.

**Expected:** with pcbnew *and* eeschema open on one project, a request
addressed to a schematic document reaches the schematic handler, regardless
of handler
author: Escain

title: Fix project state reset on unsaved profile change by using .kdenlive temp extension
description:
As I mentioned, I looked into issue #2229 and found the root cause.

When changing the profile on an unsaved project, Kdenlive saves a temp file with a .mlt extension and passes it to openFile(). isKdenliveProjectFile() fails the MIME check for .mlt and treats it as a media clip instead of a project, wiping the current project and opening a blank one.

isKdenliveProjectFile() could use a broader cleanup later, but changing the temp file extension to .kdenlive fixes this issue on its own, so I kept the PR small.

how to test this works:

* Add clips/tracks to a new unsaved project.
* Change the project profile in Project Settings for example to 1080p 30fps from 1080p 60fps.
* Verify the project reloads with everything intact instead of resetting (originally it failed to load it back in).

title: Fix the concurrency issue in the screenshot utility.
description:
# Description:

When the button was clicked, the button wasn't disabled, causing a concurrency issue with the screenshot capture and sound effect. You could click multiple times, and it would trigger multiple sound effects and save screenshots to your disk.

# Changes:

I changed the `_onCaptureButtonClicked` function, to disable the capture button and prevent multiple screenshots at the same time.

```js
            // Disable to avoid race conditions.
            this._captureButton.reactive = false;
```

I also changed the `_finishClosing` function, to enable the capture button.

# Testing:

I haven't tested yet.

title: kitemlistcontroller: select the item on a right-button double-click
description:
When right-clicking an item and then rapidly right-clicking a second item,
the general view context menu was shown instead of the second item's menu.

The rapid second click is delivered as a double-click rather than a press,
so mouseDoubleClickEvent() runs instead of mousePressEvent(). For the right
button that handler returned early without applying any selection, unlike a
single right-click which selects the item in onPress(). contextMenuEvent()
only opens an item's menu when that item is selected, so it fell back to the
view menu.

Treat a right-button double-click like a single right-click press so the item
under the cursor gets selected and the following context menu targets it.

title: Dolphinview: Refresh the default zoom level when settings are applied
description:
The per folder zoom feature stores a zoom level per folder where a
stored value of -1 means the folder follows the default from the
view mode settings. That default is cached per view in
m_defaultZoomLevel and was only refreshed when a view was created
or its view mode changed.

When the default icon size is changed in the settings dialog the
new value is saved but open views kept using the cached default so
the change only became visible after a restart.

Refresh the cached default in readSettings so views following the
default adopt the new icon size as soon as the settings dialog
applies it. Folders with a stored zoom level keep their size.

--- StaticMessages.sh

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2021 Volker Krause <vkrause@kde.org>
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: CC0-1.0
+
+# The name of catalog we create (without the.pot extension)
+# Required by scripty
+FILENAME="krita-android"
+
+# relative path to the Android resource folder
+ANDROID_RES_DIR="packaging/android/apk/res"
+
+# Called by scripty for message extraction
+# First parameter will be the path of the pot file we have to create, includes $FILENAME
+function export_pot_file
+{
+    mkdir outdir
+    ANSI_COLORS_DISABLED=1 a2po export --android $ANDROID_RES_DIR --gettext outdir
+    mv outdir/template.pot $1
+    rm -rf outdir
+    rm -f rc.cpp
+}
+
+# Called by scripty for merging messages
+# First parameter will be a path that will contain several .po files with the format LANG.po
+function import_po_files
+{
+    podir=$1
+    # Android doesn't support languages with an @
+    find "$podir" -type f -name "*@*.po" -delete
+    # drop obsolete messages, as Babel cannot parse them -- see:
+    # https://github.com/python-babel/babel/issues/206
+    # https://github.com/python-babel/babel/issues/566
+    find "$podir" -name '*.po' -exec msgattrib --no-obsolete -o {} {} \;
+    ANSI_COLORS_DISABLED=1 a2po import --ignore-fuzzy --android $ANDROID_RES_DIR --gettext $podir
+}

title: dpmsinputeventfilter: fix use-after-free in touchUp
description:
`DpmsInputEventFilter::touchUp()` calls `notify()` and then assigns to two of its own
members. `notify()` destroys the filter synchronously, so both assignments write into
freed memory:

```cpp
if (m_doubleTapTimer.elapsed() < qApp->doubleClickInterval() && !m_proximityClose) {
    notify();                        // destroys *this*
}
m_doubleTapTimer.invalidate();       // write to freed memory
m_secondTap = false;                 // write to freed memory
```

The destruction happens entirely within one call stack:

```
DpmsInputEventFilter::notify()
  -> Workspace::requestDpmsState(DpmsState::On)
     -> m_dpmsFilter.reset()
        -> ~DpmsInputEventFilter() -> ~InputEventFilter()
           -> InputRedirection::uninstallInputEventFilter(this)
           -> operator delete
```

The first commit reorders the block so that `notify()` is the last statement touching
the object. Behaviour is unchanged when `notify()` does *not* destroy the filter —
`requestDpmsState()` returns early when the outputs are already on, and in that case
both versions end with the timer invalidated and `m_secondTap` cleared.

## Why only these two paths

The filter has seventeen handlers. Fifteen follow the same shape — `notify(); return
true;` — and never touch a member afterwards, so the object being dead by then does no
harm and the loop ends immediately. Exactly two deviate, each in its own way:

- `touchUp()` writes to members after `notify()`. That is the crash, fixed by the first
  commit.
- `switchEvent()` returns `false` after `notify()`, so `processFilters()` keeps walking
  a list the filter has just removed itself from: one filter gets skipped, another gets
  called twice. No memory error, but wrong dispatch. That is what the second commit is
  for.

The second commit is not a crash fix and its message says so. Per review feedback it
is now the least intrusive form: both dispatch loops iterate over a copy of the list,
so the loop stays valid when a handler uninstalls and deletes

title: spa: v4l2: do not walk past the buffers the caller provided
description:
`spa_v4l2_use_buffers()` loops to `reqbuf.count` over `buffers[]`, which is the caller's array of
`n_buffers` entries. When `VIDIOC_REQBUFS` grants more buffers than were asked for,
`b->outbuf = buffers[i]` reads past the end of it, and `port->n_buffers` is then set to that larger
count as well. `port_use_buffers()` rejects `n_buffers > MAX_BUFFERS`, but nothing bounds
`reqbuf.count`, so a driver returning more than `MAX_BUFFERS` walks past `port->buffers[]` too.
`mmap_init()` is already bounded correctly, so this is only about `spa_v4l2_use_buffers()`.

Getting more than requested is documented behaviour, not a driver bug — and it is generic
videobuf2, not a quirk: `vb2_core_reqbufs()` allocates `max(count, q->min_reqbufs_allocation)`, and
`min_reqbufs_allocation` is raised to at least `q->min_queued_buffers + 1`. Any driver that sets
`min_queued_buffers` returns more than it was asked for whenever the request is below that floor —
reachable here, since `SPA_PARAM_Buffers` advertises `RANGE(SPA_MIN(4, max_buffers), 1, max_buffers)`.

The patch bounds the loop and the resulting count, and warns when the surplus is dropped.

Ignoring the surplus is not free, and the failure is quiet: `vb2_core_streamon()` only calls
`vb2_start_streaming()` once `q->queued_count >= q->min_queued_buffers`, so a driver that needed
those extra buffers gives a `VIDIOC_STREAMON` that succeeds and then never delivers a frame. That
is a bad outcome — but a diagnosable one with a warning next to it, which reading past the end of
the caller's array is not.

**Reproduced.** MacBookPro14,1 with facetimehd. The device supports EXPBUF, so PipeWire normally
takes the allocation path and never reaches `spa_v4l2_use_buffers()`; I made the plugin report
EXPBUF as unsupported, which is the configuration a device without it is in anyway, and changed
nothing else. `VIDIOC_REQBUFS` then returns 4 for any request below 4, so `pipewiresrc
max-buffers=2` lands exactly on `reqbuf.count(4) > n_buffers(2)`:

|
author: vrilutza

title: spa: v4l2: offer the frame size a source natively produces
description:
## Problem

A V4L2 device that answers `VIDIOC_ENUM_FRAMESIZES` with a stepwise or
continuous range is advertised with its **smallest** frame as the default. A
client that expresses no size of its own gets that, so such a camera opens at
the smallest frame it can produce — 16x16 on `vivid`. A device that enumerates
discrete sizes hands its largest frame to the same client, so the two paths do
not agree either.

The slot has to hold something, and today it holds the smallest frame the device
can be asked for, which is as much a decision as any other.

## Reproduction

```
$ sudo modprobe vivid n_devs=1 node_types=0x1
$ v4l2-ctl -d /dev/video2 --set-input=1                     # a stepwise input
$ v4l2-ctl -d /dev/video2 --list-framesizes=YUYV
	Size: Stepwise 16x16 - 16384x8640 with step 2/2
$ v4l2-ctl -d /dev/video2 --get-selection=target=crop_bounds
	Selection Video Capture: crop_bounds, Left 0, Top 0, Width 720, Height 576
```

The enumeration says 16x16 - 16384x8640; the source rectangle behind it is
720x576. What a client with no preference of its own gets:

```
$ gst-launch-1.0 -v pipewiresrc target-object=v4l2_input.platform-vivid.0 ! fakesink
... caps = video/x-raw, ..., width=(int)16, height=(int)16
```

## Change

Ask the device for its source rectangle with `VIDIOC_G_SELECTION` /
`V4L2_SEL_TGT_CROP_BOUNDS` and put that in the default, clamped to the
enumerated range and step. A device that does not answer keeps the default it
advertises today, the smallest frame.

The enumerated maximum is not usable as the answer: on a device with a scaler
the range describes what the scaler can emit, not what reaches it. `vivid`
offers 16x16 - 16384x8640 from a 720x576 source, so the maximum there is 720x576
upscaled to 141 MP — no extra detail, 283 MB per frame.

## Measured

`vivid` has two stepwise inputs that report different source rectangles behind
the same range, which makes it a self-contained test:

|                    | `CROP_BOUNDS` | before | after |
|-------

title: Make recorder writer not interrupt tool usage
description:
The race condition is:

1. Main thread checks the tool in use and requests a capture.
2. User starts a freehand selection stroke. During this, no capture is allowed.
3. Recorder thread wakes up and cancels the stroke.

The fix for this is to re-check the tool in use in step 3.

BUG:488472

Test Plan
---------

Bit hard to test because it's a race condition. Make a stroke, switch to the freehand select tool, start a selection. Depending on your device, there is enough of a delay between the capture request and the actual capture that it can interrupt you.

For artificial testing, add a sleep in RecorderWriter::Private::captureImage to make it easier to lose the race.

title: Tolerate unmapped CDot block reasons in Secrets Manager entitlement
description:
## What does this MR do and why?

GitLab asks CustomersDot (`/api/v1/consumers/resolve`) whether a namespace is allowed to use Secrets Manager. When usage is not permitted, CustomersDot responds with HTTP 402 and includes a `block_reason` in the response body. Before this change, `Gitlab::SubscriptionPortal::SecretsManagerConsumerResolveResponse` raised an `ArgumentError` for any `block_reason` outside a four-value allowlist. CustomersDot's vocabulary is wider than that allowlist, and it sends `usage_not_allowed` as its default deny — for example, for namespaces on a plan trial that have no Secrets Manager trial or credits. Because the raise happened before the client-side cache write, every request re-hit CustomersDot, generating a high volume of fail-closed exceptions in production and amplifying load on CustomersDot.

This MR makes the response object parse any `block_reason` without raising; only the response shape is still validated (a `block_reason` on a non-blocked response still raises). `usage_not_allowed` is added to the known reasons, and the entitlement resolver maps it the same way as `on_demand_disabled`: trials-eligible namespaces keep the `trial_eligible` state so the trial CTA stays reachable, active trials map to `blocked/credits_exhausted`, expired trials map to `blocked/trial_expired`, and ineligible namespaces resolve to `ineligible` silently. That combination is the expected contract for plan-trial namespaces, confirmed with the Fulfillment team.

Blocked answers the resolver cannot express — unknown reasons, or a blocked response with no reason — now fail closed to `ineligible` instead of raising, and genuinely unknown reasons are reported via `Gitlab::ErrorTracking.track_exception` so any contract drift with CustomersDot still surfaces in Sentry. Since parsing no longer raises, the response is cacheable again, which removes the repeated CustomersDot calls. Behavior for all previously mapped reasons, including the `no_billable_source_error` gr

title: Blocklist shared Pinia instance from Vue 3 infection
description:
## What does this MR do and why?

The Vue 3 migration works by "infecting" a page entrypoint's module graph so it builds under @vue/compat. `app/assets/javascripts/pinia/instance.js` is a singleton holding all Pinia store state. When it gets infected (duplicated) across the Vue 2 / Vue 3 boundary, a migrated page and any bootstraps still running under Vue 2 (for example the merge request sidebar and the review drawer) end up with separate Pinia instances. State written to one instance is invisible to the other; a component mounted under Vue 2 reads an empty store, so a value like the drafts endpoint path is undefined, causing an axios request with no URL and a runtime error. The visible symptom was the review drawer toggle failing to render, plus browser-console errors in merge request feature specs.

This MR adds `app/assets/javascripts/pinia/instance.js` to `INFECTION_BLOCKLIST` in `config/helpers/context_aliases_shared.js`, next to the other singleton state files already listed there (`breadcrumbs_state.js`, `super_sidebar/state.js`). Blocklisted files never get a `?vue3` duplicate, so both the Vue 2 and Vue 3 module graphs resolve the same singleton Pinia instance and share store state. A unit test guards against accidental removal from the blocklist.

This is a build-config change with no feature flag and no user-facing behavior change on its own; it unblocks page entrypoint Vue 3 migrations that co-load Vue 2 bootstraps sharing Pinia stores.

## How to set up and validate locally

1. Run the infection-scanner unit spec: `yarn vitest:infection-scanner run vue3_infection_shared_spec`
1. Confirm the spec passes, including the assertion that the shared Pinia instance is treated as non-infectable.

title: panvk: reduce maxImageArrayLayers from 65536 to 2048
description:
### What does this MR do and why?

<!--Describe in detail what your merge request does and why.-->

```
panvk: reduce maxImageArrayLayers from 65536 to 2048

vktApiExternalMemoryTests queries
vkGetPhysicalDeviceImageFormatProperties2 to obtain maxArrayLayers and
then repeatedly allocates AHardwareBuffers using maxArrayLayers as the
layer count. With maxArrayLayers=65536, each 64x64 RGB888 buffer
requires 768 MB. The repeated large memory allocations increase memory
pressure, causing allocation latency to grow and eventually triggering
a dEQP watchdog timeout.

According to VP_ANDROID_16_minimums.json, the minimum required value is
2048. Reduce maxImageArrayLayers from 65536 to 2048 in both
VkPhysicalDeviceLimits and VkImageFormatProperties to match Android 16
minimum requirement and ensure CTS passes.

Test:
dEQP-VK.api.external.memory.android_hardware_buffer.ahb_format_properties.image_formats#*
dEQP-VK.api.external.memory.android_hardware_buffer.ahb_format_properties_2.image_formats#*

Signed-off-by: Jessie Hao <juan.hao@nxp.com>
```

title: timeremap: add keyframe type support and curve visualization to RemapView
description:
Adds per-keyframe interpolation types to the Time Remapping panel, so speed changes can ease in and out instead of switching abruptly at every keyframe boundary. Each keyframe can be set to its own interpolation type from a new Type selector, and a curve band showing the actual interpolated shape is drawn between the existing input and output rulers.

The selector offers the 13 interpolation types the effect stack already uses elsewhere, which is everything in `KeyframeModel::getKeyframeTypes()` apart from the deprecated Curve entry. Bounce and elastic are worth calling out: they overshoot the keyframe value, and on a time map an overshoot means source time briefly runs backwards, so the clip plays in reverse for a few frames around the keyframe. Measured against MLT over a 50 frame span, bounce runs backwards for 16 frames and elastic for 23, with elastic also reaching source positions outside the clip's own duration. They are included because that behavior is usable on purpose, and are listed last so the well behaved types come first. Exponential and circular were expected to overshoot as well but measured clean, staying monotonic and in range.

## What changed

* Each keyframe stores its own interpolation type, keyed by output position in `m_keyframeTypes`. An absent key means linear, so existing projects load as all linear with no migration step
* Types are serialized through MLT's own animation API (`anim_set` with an `mlt_keyframe_type`, then `serialize_cut`) rather than by hand, so the `time_map` string stays in whatever format MLT expects. Parsing reads the type back with `Mlt::Animation::key_get`
* A Type combo box in the remap dialog sets the type of the currently selected keyframe, and follows the selection as it changes
* The curve is sampled per pixel from the parsed `time_map` animation, so what is drawn is what MLT will actually play back rather than a redrawn approximation of the keyframe values
* The curve is drawn between the two rulers as an addit

title: Add extensions that let a client react to global input triggers.
description:
An action is a named activity a client performs (for example "play/pause" or
"mute"); a trigger is the input that fires it (for example Meta+P). The two
extensions connect them:

- `ext_input_trigger_registration_v1` is used by a privileged client to register
  actions and bind them to triggers.
- `ext_input_trigger_action_v1` is used by any client to subscribe to a
  registered action and receive notifications when it occurs. Subscription
  uses a token issued during registration, used either by the registering
  client itself or by an unprivileged client that has been passed the token
  out of band.

For example, a media player subscribes to the system "play/pause" action and
toggles playback whenever the key is pressed — without ever holding keyboard
focus. Each notification carries an `xdg_activation_v1` token, so a client can
grab focus when it needs to (as an application switcher or launcher would).

Splitting a privileged registration side from an unprivileged subscription side
lets a "gatekeeper" (for example a portal backend) own policy, security and any
user-facing UI, keeping the compositor policy-free.

This is useful for real applications. Media keys, push-to-talk (VoIP, Discord),
toggle-record (OBS) and Alt-Tab-style switchers all require reacting to input
the client is not focused for — something Wayland offers no way to do today.

Having a standard protocol benefits the whole ecosystem. A single gatekeeper or
portal backend works across every compositor, instead of each one reinventing
global-shortcut plumbing. These extensions are also a natural backend for the
existing DBus GlobalShortcuts portal, which deliberately leaves compositor
integration undefined and is keyboard-only.

This enables correct focus behavior. Delivering an `xdg_activation_v1` token
with each event lets a notified client take focus cleanly — awkward to do
over DBus alone.

These extensions are device-agnostic. Triggers are not limited to the keyboard;
the design extends to poin

title: meta-a11y-manager: Add a method to return the current locked modifiers
description:
We're sending the current modifiers with each key event, but we do not
have a way how to query them before one. That causes some key binding
regressions in Orca's key binding heuristics, namely orca#743.

Helps at-spi2-core#238.
author: tyrylu
diff:
--- data/dbus-interfaces/org.freedesktop.a11y.xml
+++ data/dbus-interfaces/org.freedesktop.a11y.xml
@@ -98,6 +98,19 @@
       <arg type="a(uu)" name="keystrokes" direction="in" />
     </method>
 
+    <!--
+        GetLockedModifiers:
+        @state: XKB modifier mask for currently locked modifiers
+
+        Returns the XKB modifier mask of modifiers that are currently in
+        the locked state, for example Num Lock or Caps Lock, or as a
+        result of sticky keys. This allows clients to query the initial
+        locked modifier state before the first KeyEvent is received.
+    -->
+    <method name="GetLockedModifiers">
+      <arg type="u" name="state" direction="out"/>
+    </method>
+
     <!--
         KeyEvent:
         @released: whether this is a key-up event
--- src/backends/meta-a11y-manager.c
+++ src/backends/meta-a11y-manager.c
@@ -332,6 +332,25 @@ handle_set_key_grabs (MetaDBusKeyboardMonitor *skeleton,
   return G_DBUS_METHOD_INVOCATION_HANDLED;
 }
 
+static gboolean
+handle_get_locked_modifiers (MetaDBusKeyboardMonitor *skeleton,
+                             GDBusMethodInvocation   *invocation,
+                             MetaA11yManager         *a11y_manager)
+{
+  ClutterBackend *clutter_backend =
+    meta_backend_get_clutter_backend (a11y_manager->backend);
+  ClutterSeat *seat =
+    clutter_backend_get_default_seat (clutter_backend);
+  ClutterKeymap *keymap = clutter_seat_get_keymap (seat);
+  xkb_mod_mask_t depressed, latched, locked;
+
+  clutter_keymap_get_modifier_state (keymap, &depressed, &latched, &locked);
+
+  meta_dbus_keyboard_monitor_complete_get_locked_modifiers (
+    skeleton, invocation, locked);
+  return G_DBUS_METHOD_INVOCATION_HANDLED;
+}
+
 static gboolean
 handle_query_pointer (MetaDBusPointerLocator *skeleton,
                       GDBusMethodInvocation  *invocation,
@@ -388,6 +407,8 @@ on_bus_acquired (GDBusConnection *connection,

   g_signal_connect (manager->keyboard_monitor_skeleton, "handle-set-key-grabs",

+  g_signal_connect (manager->keyboard_monitor_skeleton, "handle-get-locked-modifiers",

title: gdk/win32: Fixed Black transparent areas for OpenGL, refreshing when window was off desktop, buggy state handling and improper positioning calls, previews in the taskbar
description:
When hovering over the taskbar preview, two windows were shown, even if the GPU window is cloaked. It had to be removed from "PEEK". 

Fixed the black transparent corners for OpenGL with a DwmEnableBlurBehindWindow call. Note that it was already present on the main window.

Presenting does not update the WM visual that is outside the desktop. This leads to glitched visuals when they are moved back into the desktop. The fix is to move the cloaked rendering window with the application window and use invalid regions from Winapi to invalidate our gdk surface. This is still not ideal as there can be temporary glitching until a frame is pushed to the screen. Note that at least on Vulkan, this is not a driver bug. It is caused by GTK code because I can't reproduce the same issue in my custom Vulkan test app. I did not investigate OpenGL.

Note that there is no reason to use Direct composition for Vulkan and OpenGL backends because it just causes issues. And OpenGL/Vulkan presenting should not be limited to the surface area that is inside the desktop view. I did not find the code that caused it.

title: eeschema: sort design blocks alphabetically in the Design Blocks panel
description:
DESIGN_BLOCK_TREE_MODEL_ADAPTER passed `presorted=true` to `DoAddLibrary()`, but `getDesignBlocks()` returns blocks in filesystem enumeration order (name-hash order on APFS), so the panel showed them effectively randomly. Pass `presorted=false` so `AssignIntrinsicRanks()` applies the natural sort, matching the symbol chooser.

The footprint tree also passes `true`, but its list is sorted upstream — design blocks have no such sorting anywhere in the chain.

Verified on macOS (Apple Silicon, 10.0 branch build): a library whose on-disk enumeration order differs from name order now lists alphabetically.

title: harden PCB_EDITOR_CONDITIONS display helpers
description:
### Context

This patch is part of a series that came out of building **KICAD_MCP**, an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server that lets
LLM agents drive a live KiCad session through KiCad's official IPC API — the
protobuf-over-socket interface that also backs `kicad-python`/`kipy`. The
agent does what a plugin would do, only continuously and headlessly: place
symbols and footprints, wire up hierarchical sheets, run ERC, update the PCB
from the schematic — all as `CreateItems` / `GetItems` / `UpdateItems` /
`SaveDocument` / … protobuf requests.

Driving the API at that intensity exercises paths no interactive session
hits: documents that are open but not displayed, sheets other than the active
one, both editors open against the same project, round-trips through the
clipboard S-expression format, and error paths that must come back as
protobuf statuses rather than dialogs (an IPC client cannot click "OK", so
any modal dialog reached from a handler hangs the client). A typical session
that surfaced several of the bugs in this series at once:

> create a sub-sheet → place a resistor on it while the root sheet is
> displayed → save all → run ERC from `kicad-cli` — each step crossed a
> different bug fixed below.

The branches are cut against `master` and are independent of each other
unless the section says otherwise.

### Authorship

The code was co-authored and reviewed with LLM assistance (**Claude-Fable-5** and **GLM**-5.1), under human direction, code-revision, and validated by
a human against a live KiCad build. Every branch compiles clean (Release,
`-DKICAD_BUILD_QA_TESTS=ON`) and went through two adversarial review rounds
before submission.

---

**Function:** the eight static display-flag helpers in
`pcbnew/tools/pcb_editor_conditions.cpp`
(`padFillDisplayFunc`, `textFillDisplayFunc`, `zoneDisplayModeFunc`, …) used
as `wxUpdateUIEvent` conditions.

**Background:** during IPC testing, a reproducible segfault was observed with
`PCB_EDITOR_CONDITIONS::padFillDisplayF

This protocol allows clients to learn the current screen orientation as well as request the orientation to be set.

For now I've chosen for this to be an RFC since I have not authored a wayland protocol yet and I'm unsure if this is the best way to do it.

### Use cases

* Camera application needs to know screen orientation for landscape/portrait photos
* Games may want to always be displayed in landscape orientation
* Video players may want to go into landscape mode if the video aspect ratio calls for it

@agx

I haven't found if there are any other maintainers of mobile shells which contribute here. 

Merge requirements:

* [ ] 2 ACKs

* [ ] one client implementation

title: pcbnew: fix footprint properties 3D model crash
description:
## Change Description

This fixes a crash in the Footprint Editor when accepting Footprint Properties after opening the 3D Models tab or changing a 3D model path.

The Footprint Editor properties dialog previously rebuilt the footprint field list by removing all existing fields and creating new field objects from the dialog grid. During commit damage propagation, KiCad calculates the footprint bounding box for the modified footprint. If mandatory fields had just been removed and recreated, the footprint could be left with invalid or missing mandatory field objects while `Reference()` or `Value()` were dereferenced by `GetBoundingBox()`.

The fix updates mandatory fields in place and only rebuilds user fields. This keeps the mandatory field objects stable while still applying edited field data and preserving the previous user-field behavior.

Fixes #25239

## Verification

- Built `pcbnew` and `kicad` in Debug on Windows.

- Manually verified changing the 3D model path persists after reopening properties.

-->

### Original commit message(s)

* libtaskmanager: add a TaskGroupingProxyModel stress test

Exercises the grouping model over the same stack shape as the live one
(concatenated sources -> filter -> grouping) with randomized, deterministically
seeded add/remove/batch/attention/appid/filter/group-mode operations. After each
step it checks that every proxy index maps to a unique, in-range source row, and
QAbstractItemModelTester validates that the model's row signals stay consistent.

There was no TaskGroupingProxyModel test before; this guards its index mapping
and signal correctness against regressions.

CCBUG: 506562

* libtaskmanager: assert TaskGroupingProxyModel's rowMap invariant in debug builds

rowMap must partition exactly the source rows: every source row present once, in
range, and no empty group. When it silently falls out of sync, the stale entry
only surfaces much later as a crash in mapToSource() and the source proxies.

Check the invariant at the end of every rowMap mutation, so in a debug build a
handler that corrupts it aborts right there with a backtrace naming it, instead
of crashing elsewhere. Compiled out (QT_NO_DEBUG) in release builds.

CCBUG: 506562

* libtaskmanager: guard TaskGroupingProxyModel::mapToSource against stale rows

rowMap holds source row numbers maintained by hand across source inserts and
removals. When it falls out of sync so an entry points past the current source
model, mapToSource() handed an out-of-range row to the source proxies: the group
aggregation in data() (all()/any() and the per-role child loops) then called
data() on that index, QSortFilterProxyModel::mapToSource ran
QConcatenateTablesProxyModel::index() out of bounds and crashed.

title: Release onscreens when there are no views left
description:
Detached onscreens are normally released when a view posts the pending mode set. If no views are left (p.ex. last connector lost all its modes) then no frame will ever be posted and the scanout buffers linger until the renderer is disposed. We simply release them if there are no views left.

We release the detached onscreens at the end of the rebuild, because by then there are no views left to ever complete the pending mode set.

Closes https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/mutter/-/work_items/4920

title: Rectangles can be flipped by dragging the corners
description:
This fixes #6368

This is done by adapting both RectKnotHolderEntityWH and
RectKnotHolderEntityXY. The general idea is that when we would like to
set a negative width or height we instead "swap" the corner represented
by (rect->x,rect->y) and then assign the absolute value of the width or
heigth.

Note that this changes some invariants on those classes, namely:
- for RectKnotHolderEntityXY we could assume that (rect->x, rect->y)
  was always the corner dragged, but that's not true anymore once the
  cursor is moving on the right on what was initially the opposite edge.
  Said differently we could assume that `opposite_x` and `opposite_y`
  was a constant -and could hence be re-computed every time the cursor
  moved (sure, it was a small waste of CPU cycle, but it always gave the
  same result)
- similarly, for RectKnotHolderEntityWH we could assume that (rect->x,
  rect->y) never moved, which made the code easier.

It is not a big deal to not have those invariants anymore given that
they were "private invariant", not exposed to the outside of this class.
But it still means that we have to keep track of some state, as can be
seen by the private fields added on those classes.
Those states are initialized when the user starts to drag, ie in
`knot_grabbed`.

Note that, now that those classes have a state, we could probably, in a
future commit, leverage it to avoid some useless recomputations. Namely:
in RectKnotHolderEntityWH::set_internal (when the user presses CONTROL)
we recompute each time w_orig, h_orig, and ratio, even though the input
is constant. (I'm not doing it in this commit to avoid having a too big
one)

/!\ Subtelty to have in mind to review this commit: there are a couple
of lines in RectKnotHolderEntityWH::set_internal that change like this
and it may seem weird:

- rect->height = MAX(h_orig + minx / ratio, 0);
+ set_signed_height(origin[Geom::Y] - rect->y.computed + minx / ratio);

it may seems weird that we're replacing `h_orig` by that more
complicat

title: pipewire: module-rt: do async dbus calls with rtkit
description:
Occasionally rtkit / xdg realtime portal fails to return the property values
(`org.freedesktop.DBus.Properties.Get()`) within the default libdbus timeout
(25 seconds). While this does not affect the main loop because it runs in a
separate thread, it can still blocks shutdown, which is inconvenient when using
e.g. `pw-dump` or `pw-mon`, especially since the properties are queried
sequentially. (Note that rtkit has only recently gained support for retrieving
all properties of an interface, so that cannot yet be used.)

Furthermore, the replies to the actual `MakeThreadRealtimeWithPID()` and
`MakeThreadHighPriorityWithPID()` calls are not received since 09277cbf
("module-rt: don't block on method calls").

This change addresses both by switching to the `DBusPendingCall` interface.
This allows immediate shutdown by cancelling the pending calls without any
waiting, and enables the reporting of error replies in the log.

See !2844

title: Reconcile VAC mid-skew default-branch findings
description:
## What does this MR do and why?

This is the **reconciliation** part of the durable fix for #613547 (parent bug #612930, epic gitlab-org&3430).

The store-phase failsafe (guarantee the default context exists before the store phase, !251594) and the dismissal carry-over already landed on master. What remained open on #613547 is **Part 2: reconcile the findings that were stored before the default context existed**, plus its sizing.

### Background

Before a VAC project's default tracked context exists, its first default-branch pipelines resolve the tracked context find-only, get `nil`, and store findings with the context-unaware (v1) UUID and a `NULL` `security_project_tracked_context_id`. Once the v2 default context exists, a fresh default-branch scan computes the context-aware (v2) UUID and no longer matches those rows, so the same vulnerability opens a second time and the stale v1 row auto-resolves.

Findings that were **dropped on ingestion** in #612930 are **not** in scope: they were never persisted, so a rescan re-detects them (agreed position, no repair migration for the drop). This MR only repairs findings that **were** persisted on the default branch under the stale scheme, so stored data lines up with the v2 default context. It **does not** change any tracked context's `uuid_version`, and it never touches findings already keyed to a real context, so legitimate non-default-branch findings are left alone.

### What this adds

- `Security::ProjectTrackedContexts::ReconcileNullContextDefaultFindingsService`:
  - `#affected_finding_count` — read-only sizing (safe without the flag); applies the same eligibility as `#execute`, so the number matches what would actually be repaired.
  - `#execute` — idempotent, batched re-key of the NULL-context default-branch findings to the v2 default context.
- Gated behind `vac_reconcile_null_context_findings` (default off). **Deliberately not scheduled** — the affected population is measured first, then the repair is run delibe

title: filechooserwidget: stop the location and load timeouts in dispose
description:
`gtk_file_chooser_widget_dispose()` stops the widget's pending async work
through `cancel_all_operations()`, but `location_changed_id` and
`load_timeout_id` are left out of it and removed in finalize instead.

Dispose and finalize are the same instant only when nobody else holds a
reference. `gtk_widget_destroy()` documents that a widget with outstanding
references is left in an `"inert"` state. In that window dispose has already
destroyed the template children, but the private pointers to them are never
cleared, so a timeout that survives into the gap runs against destroyed widgets:

- `location_changed_timeout_cb()` reaches `check_preview_change()`, which reads
  `priv->browse_files_tree_view` and calls `gtk_label_set_text()` on
  `priv->preview_label`.
- `load_timeout_cb()` reaches `load_set_model()`, which calls
  `gtk_tree_view_set_model()` on `priv->browse_files_tree_view`.

Any caller that holds its reference longer than the timeout's remaining delay
hits this.

This patch moves both removals into dispose. `show_progress_timeout` and
`load_recent_id` are already covered there through `search_stop_searching()` and
`recent_stop_loading()`; these two were the only ones left out.

I have a standalone test program — plain GTK3, public API only — that hits this
on 3.24.32 and on current `gtk-3-24`, and can post it if that would help.

Two notes on the diff:

- In `gtk_file_chooser_widget_finalize()` I turned the `location_changed_id`
  removal into `g_assert (priv->location_changed_id == 0)` rather than deleting
  it, so a path that arms the timeout after dispose does not go unnoticed. Happy
  to drop it.
- The `main` branch removes `location_changed_id` in finalize too. Glad to send
  a matching patch.

title: ZigBee ZCL Touchlink: empty the commissioning map on a redissect.
description:
All of the entries in the commissioning map are allocated with "file"
scope, which means that, before a redissect pass, they will all be
freed.

On a dissection init, empty the map, so that we don't have a bunch of
references to freed memory and thus don't have a use-after-free issue.

Observed when loading the ALL_ENCAPS_HOLY_GRAIL_PACP.pcapng file from
https://github.com/SharonBrizinov/Holy-Grail-PCAP; that file has a DSB
that's not at the beginning of the file, so a redissect is queued after
reading the file in. It results in a crash on macOS Tahoe - memory
allocators are free to release regions of the address space that no
longer contain any allocated data, and some do, so use-after-free can
mean you get a "that address is not valid" trap.

title: docs: describe initrd profile propagation in nm-initrd-generator(8)
description:
## Summary

Adds a "Propagation to the real root" section to `nm-initrd-generator(8)`.

## Purpose

The initrd-to-real-root propagation exists for a good reason (a system whose root filesystem is on the network must not have its connectivity interrupted at pivot), but it is documented nowhere, and on a machine that boots from local storage it is usually unwanted. The result is that administrators find the leftover profiles in `nmcli connection show`, cannot tell what they are, and go looking for a way to turn them off.

This was raised upstream in https://github.com/dracutdevs/dracut/issues/1062. The conclusion there, was that since the configuration is NetworkManager-specific it belongs in the `nm-initrd-generator` man page rather than in `dracut.cmdline`. 

Resolves: https://issues.redhat.com/browse/RHEL-186231

## Checklist

Please read https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/NetworkManager/NetworkManager/-/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md before opening the merge request. In particular, check that:

- [x] The subject for all commits is concise, explanatory, and includes a prefix indicating the area of code changed (e.g., "nmcli: ", "core: ")
- [x] The message for all commits explains the reason for the change
- [x] The source is properly formatted
- [x] Any relevant documentation is up to date
- [x] You have added unit tests if applicable
- [x] The NEWS file is updated when the change deserves to be mentioned, for example for new features, behavior changes, API deprecations, etc.
author: josie
diff:
--- man/nm-initrd-generator.xml
+++ man/nm-initrd-generator.xml
@@ -440,6 +440,50 @@
     </itemizedlist>
   </refsect1>
 
+  <refsect1 id='real_root'><title>Propagation to the real root</title>
+
+    <para>The profiles are written to
+    <filename>&nmrundir;/system-connections</filename> and are tagged
+    with the <literal>org.freedesktop.NetworkManager.origin</literal> user
+    setting, whose value is <literal>nm-initrd-generator</literal>.</para>
+
+    <para><filename>/run</filename> is carried over when the initrd switches to
+    the real root, so those profiles are still there when the second
+    NetworkManager instance starts. It reads them and keeps the interfaces
+    configured as the initrd left them. This is deliberate: it is what allows a
+    system whose root filesystem is on the network to switch root without
+    interrupting connectivity.</para>
+
+    <para>On a system that boots from local storage the propagation is usually
+    not wanted, because the persistent profiles in
+    <filename>&sysconfdir;/NetworkManager/system-connections</filename> are meant to take over.
+    To suppress it, drop a file in
+    <filename>&sysconfdir;/NetworkManager/conf.d</filename> containing:</para>
+
+<programlisting>
+[device]
+keep-configuration=no
+allowed-connections=except:origin:nm-initrd-generator
+</programlisting>
+
+    <para><literal>keep-configuration=no</literal> stops NetworkManager from
+    adopting the existing interface configuration, so it activates the most
+    suitable persistent profile instead;
+    <literal>allowed-connections</literal> then prevents the initrd profiles
+    from being activated at all. Both keys are described in <link
+    linkend='NetworkManager.conf'><citerefentry><refentrytitle>NetworkManager.conf</refentrytitle><manvolnum>5</manvolnum></citerefentry></link>.
+    A <literal>[device]</literal> section without a
+    <literal>match-device</literal> key applies to every device; add one only
+    to restrict the setting to particular interfaces.</para>
+
+    <para>This stops the initrd profiles from being used, but does not remove
+    them. They stay visible as inactive profiles in
+    <command>nmcli connection show</command> until the next boot, since
+    <filename>/run</filename> does not survive a reboot. To remove them
+    earlier, delete them with <command>nmcli connection delete</command>.</para>
+
+  </refsect1>
+
   <refsect1 id='exit_status'><title>Exit Status</title>
     <para><command>nm-initrd-generator</command> exits with status 0. It ignores unrecognized
     options and prints an error message if it encounters a malformed option.</para>

title: wifi: don't scan while the P2P device on the same phy is activating
description:
## Summary

Stop a Wi-Fi device from scanning while the Wi-Fi P2P device on the same radio is activating, and keep it from scanning for another SCAN_INTERVAL_SEC_MIN once that ends.

Scanning is suppressed per device, so a disconnected wlan0 keeps scanning while the wifi-p2p device on the same phy runs discovery, GO negotiation and DHCP. title: Fix effect keyframes scaling and timeline display on clip speed change
description:
When changing a clip's speed, effect keyframes (e.g. Transform, Position and Zoom) were previously trimmed as if the clip edges had been resized, leaving keyframes desynchronized or lost on split clips. This fix introduces dedicated keyframe scaling across the effect stack on timewarp producer changes, correctly maps 2D point parameters to avoid invalid timeline curve selection, guards against integer rounding when resetting speed to 100%, and fixes NaN tooltips on timeline keyframe delegates.

title: SAP dissectors: Harden dissectors against malformed packet lengths
description:
Tighten SAP protocol dissectors so truncated or inconsistent packet
lengths are handled as malformed input instead of driving unchecked
offsets, string scans, or oversized subtree lengths. Also consolidate
bit-flag display with proto_tree_add_bitmask() where the fields are
true flag groups.

packet-sapdiag.c:
- Convert request-info, support-bits, dynamic atom attribute, UI event,
  COM flag, and header flag fields to proto_tree_add_bitmask() arrays.
- Preserve existing flag names and bit positions while displaying flags
  through the standard bitmask subtree pattern.
- Add an early short-header guard before decoding the Diag header flags.

packet-sapenqueue.c:
- Add shared length validation for server-admin and connection-admin
  structures.
- Report malformed truncated admin headers, trace requests, parameter
  counts, parameter IDs, parameter lengths, and parameter values.
- Clamp variable trace pattern lengths to available packet data.

packet-saphdb.c:
- Bound authentication and GSS authentication field parsing by the
  containing part length.
- Add malformed expert info for truncated field counts, extended length
  headers, and field payloads.
- Limit segment and message loops to the advertised buffer bounds and
  captured remaining data.

packet-sapigs.c:
- Add captured-length checks around fixed ASCII fields and table metadata.
- Stop decoding incomplete headers and command bodies before fixed-width
  reads.
- Only add payload data when the declared length is fully available.

packet-sapms.c:
- Convert message-type flag groups to proto_tree_add_bitmask().
- Add short-header checks for MS, opcode, and ADM headers.
- Validate opcode body lengths, variable string lengths, IP-to-name
  payloads, logon fields, client fields, and null-terminated ACL entries.

packet-sapni.c:
- Clamp payload dissection length to the captured bytes available after
  the SAP NI header.
- Return the consumed header plus bounded payload length.

packet-saprfc.c:
- Reject packets shorter

## What does this MR do and why?

This MR is step 4, the last step, of the filtered search bar migration for Issues Analytics.

The legacy filtered search bar lives in `app/assets/javascripts/filtered_search/`. It uses the `FilteredSearchManager` class. This MR replaces it with the Vue component `vue_shared/components/filtered_search_bar/filtered_search_bar_root.vue`.

Earlier steps did the same migration for other pages:
- https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/merge_requests/251854
- https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/merge_requests/251857
- https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/merge_requests/251858

Each step of this migration is independent, so this MR targets `master`.

The page migrated here is Issues Analytics. One Vue component serves both the group route and the project route.

The change sits behind a new feature flag, `vue_issues_analytics_filtered_search`. The flag type is `wip`. The flag is off by default. It is an EE flag. The actor is the group or the project.

### Component changes

- `issues_analytics.vue` used to build a `FilteredSearchIssueAnalytics` object in its `created()` hook. The Haml view rendered the bar itself, outside the Vue app.
- The new bar is a child component, `ee/app/assets/javascripts/issues_analytics/components/filtered_search.vue`. It renders inside the Vue app template.
- The two views, `ee/app/views/groups/issues_analytics/show.html.haml` and `ee/app/views/projects/analytics/issues_analytics/show.html.haml`, render the old partial only when the flag is off.
- The new component picks its render path from the `filterBlockEl` prop. This prop holds the legacy bar element. When the prop is absent, the Vue bar renders itself.

title: gst: two defects in the conversion from a SPA choice to GstCaps
description:
Two things go wrong in the same place, `gstpipewireformat.c`, when a SPA choice becomes GStreamer caps. They were briefly two MRs; they rewrite the same lines and the second needs the first, so they are one.

## 1. A fraction that does not fit is silently dropped

A SPA fraction is a pair of `uint32`; a `GstFraction` is a pair of `gint`. The values were passed on unchecked, so a denominator above `INT32_MAX` arrived negative and `gst_caps_set_simple()` refused the range:

```
gst_value_collect_fraction_range: assertion 'gst_util_fraction_compare (...) < 0' failed
range start is not smaller than end for `GstFractionRange'
```

The whole `framerate` field is then missing from the caps.

It is reachable from an ordinary driver. A V4L2 source reporting a long maximum frame interval inverts into a small framerate whose denominator is that interval's numerator. `v4l2loopback` uses `UINT32_MAX` there, and so does **`drivers/media/pci/mgb4/mgb4_vin.c`**, an in-tree capture driver, where `0xFFFFFFFF / MGB4_HW_FREQ` is an unremarkable slowest frame of **34 seconds**. The value is not silly; it is the denominator of the resulting framerate that does not fit.

Reduce the fraction first, which is exact and enough for `mgb4` — the gcd is 5, so `125000000/4294967295` becomes `25000000/858993459` — and scale only when that still does not fit, which is `v4l2loopback`'s irreducible `1/UINT32_MAX`.

## 2. The value a source says it prefers is thrown away

A choice carries a preferred value in `values[0]` and the bounds after it. The conversion kept the bounds and dropped the preference, and `gst_caps_fixate()` resolves a range to its minimum — so anything fixating the caps of a PipeWire device landed at the bottom of every range.

Not on the negotiation path: `gst_pipewire_src_negotiate()` does not fixate, it hands the caps to `pw_stream_connect()` as a filter and the server picks. I checked, because I had assumed otherwise. It is the caps a `GstDeviceMonitor` reports, built in `gstpi

title: bluez5: resolve issue where LDAC ABR mode fails to reach HQ bitrate
description:
There was an issue where the LDAC ABR mode failed to reach the HQ bitrate. (The bitrate was calculated by extracting the payload size through btmon. Although there is a slight difference from the actual bitrate, it was sufficient to distinguish between HQ, SQ, and MQ bitrates.) As mentioned in the previous merge request, it successfully reached HQ and played normally when set to ABR using the Alternative A2DP Driver on Windows.

Looking into the cause, to upgrade to the HQ bitrate (or upgrade to a higher bitrate) in the LDAC ABR library, the TxQueueDepth must be 0 for a certain period of time (according to the comments in ldacBT_abr.c, converting the observing count required for HQ into time equals 5 seconds). As a result of checking by adding custom logs (tracking timestamp, unsent / LDAC_ABR_MAX_PACKET_NBYTES), packets for transmission always partially remained in the buffer, making the TxQueueDepth 1, so the zero-TxQueueDepth duration mostly lasted only around 1 to 2 seconds. To solve this, a baseline of 1 was subtracted from the packet count, and it was confirmed that HQ was reached.

However, when transmission delays occurred after reaching HQ, the buffer filled up too quickly and caused audio stuttering before the bitrate could drop to SQ or MQ. (This is the part where I misidentified the root cause in my previous merge request.) To solve this, LDAC_ABR_THRESHOLD_SAFETY_FOR_HQSQ was lowered to 2.

After applying the changes, it was confirmed that it normally reaches HQ, and when a transmission delay occurs, the audio plays smoothly by appropriately lowering the bitrate without stuttering.

title: broadcom/compiler: rebuild liveness once per spill batch
description:
### What does this MR do and why?

<!--Describe in detail what your merge request does and why.-->

```
Adaptive spilling already selects and rewrites several victims before
recoloring, but v3d_spill_reg() still rebuilt global liveness and extended
the interference graph after every victim.

On accumulator-free V3D 7.x, make spill-created temporaries costless and
unspillable, reset each victim node immediately, and defer liveness plus
temp-temp graph completion until the batch ends. Keep V3D 4.x on the
per-victim path because injected thread switches can change accumulator
classes.

Spill rewriting preserves the CFG and the relative order of unspilled old
temp occurrences. Inserted spill/fill instructions may move interval numbers,
but they cannot change old-old overlap, so existing old-old interference
edges remain valid. Temps created by rewriting need edges against the live
temps they overlap. TMU spilling is the old-temp exception: it adds uses of
spill_base, whose interval can grow and require additional edges.

While a batch is being rewritten, interference edges for spill-created temps
and new spill_base overlaps are not added yet. Later victim selection can
therefore read adjacency without those edges and choose a different victim
order and codegen. No ra_allocate() runs in that state; v3d_update_spill_graph()
recomputes liveness and adds the missing edges before the next coloring
attempt.

A transient exhaustive check matched final temp-temp adjacency against
recomputed liveness on the four spill-heavy shaders exercising this path.

On Raspberry Pi 5, shader-db -j1 pinned to one 2.8 GHz core improved from
87.566 s to 74.697 s over three runs each (-14.7%).

Shader-db changes final codegen for 4 fragment shaders out of 11,230 matched
shaders. All four produce shorter QPU streams (-44 instructions total), with
unchanged spill/fill counts. Inspection shows the underlying ALU operations
and signals are unchanged; the different spill-victim ordering changes

title: backends: clear is_primary on non-primary logical monitors
description:
# MR: backends: clear is_primary on non-primary logical monitors

## Summary

`MetaLogicalMonitor.is_primary` is sticky: it is only ever set via `meta_logical_monitor_make_primary()` and never cleared. When the primary display is changed (e.g. from gnome-control-center's Displays panel), the old primary logical monitor keeps `is_primary` set, so `org.gnome.Mutter.DisplayConfig.GetCurrentState()` reports **two** logical monitors as primary.

gnome-control-center's display panel (`cc-display-config.c`) iterates the logical monitors and keeps the **last** one marked primary, so the panel shows the wrong primary display — even though the shell itself behaves correctly (it reads `manager->primary_logical_monitor`, which points at the new primary).

## Repro steps

1. Two displays connected: built-in panel (eDP-1) + external monitor (DP-1).
2. Open Settings → Displays, set the external monitor (DP-1) as primary, Apply.
3. Expected: panel shows DP-1 as primary.
4. Actual: the top bar / activities move to DP-1 (correct), but the panel still shows eDP-1 as primary.

Observed state from `GetCurrentState` after applying:

```
logical monitor DP-1  is-primary: true   <- new primary
logical monitor eDP-1 is-primary: true   <- stale, never cleared
```

## Root cause

- `meta_logical_monitor_make_primary()` only ever sets `is_primary = TRUE`.
- There is no code path that clears it.
- `meta_logical_monitor_update()` reuses the existing `MetaLogicalMonitor` objects when the layout is unchanged and does not touch the flag, so the stale flag survives monitor reconfiguration.
- `meta_monitor_manager_set_primary_logical_monitor()` is the single place where the primary is (re)assigned; it marks the new primary but never unmarks the old one.

## Fix

In `meta_monitor_manager_set_primary_logical_monitor()`, clear `is_primary` on every other logical monitor before marking the new primary:

- add `meta_logical_monitor_clear_primary()` (symmetric to `meta_logical_monitor_make_primary()`);
